title: Gold Demand Trends: India Focus Q3 2026
gist: India's Q3 2026 gold demand fell 29% y/y to 162t but rose 3% in rupee value to INR2,419bn, with domestic prices up 45% y/y. The May duty hike to 15% pushed unofficial inflows to about 50t and a record US$43/oz discount to import parity, while RBI buying has stalled at 0.3t year-to-date and investment demand (-4% 9M) is proving stickier than jewellery (-18%).

insights.claim: India's Q3 2026 gold demand was 162t, down 29% y/y and 12% y-t-d, yet value rose 3% y/y to INR2,419bn and 38% y-t-d to INR6,688bn, so Indian buyers keep allocating more money to gold while buying fewer tonnes.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Tonnage-based demand reads understate Indian gold flows in currency terms; the price-elastic volume drop does not mean falling commitment.
insights.quote: consumers and investors continued to allocate substantial sums to gold even as higher prices resulted in lower quantities purchased

insights.claim: Indian domestic gold averaged INR148,891/10g in Q3, up 45% y/y versus only 23% for the international price (US$4,262/oz average), because rupee weakness and a higher import duty amplified the local price.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Local-currency and policy effects roughly double the affordability shock for Indian buyers versus the dollar gold move.

insights.claim: The international gold price has been easing from its January peak: the Q3 average of US$4,262/oz was down 5% q/q after US$4,506 in Q2 and US$4,873 in Q1.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Gold is consolidating well above US$4,000 rather than collapsing; India demand is recovering on dips.
insights.quote: During Q3 the gold price continued to ease from its January peak.

insights.claim: Indian jewellery value rose 16% y/y in Q3 and 29% over nine months while tonnes fell 18%; the value gain was entirely price-led, and listed jewellers' July-September revenue growth confirms value outperforming volume.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Jeweller earnings can grow on price even as unit demand shrinks, but that growth depends on prices holding up.
insights.quote: The increase in value was entirely price-led; consumers spent more despite buying less gold.

themes.theme: Duty hike and the unofficial import channel

insights.claim: India's May import duty increase to 15% (a nine-percentage-point hike from 6%) pushed unofficial gold inflows to about 50t in Q3 from just 3t a year earlier, diverting supply from official channels.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Duty hikes shift gold into smuggling rather than eliminating demand; official import and trade-balance statistics will understate true gold absorption.
insights.quote: has increased the incentive for inflows through unofficial channels

insights.claim: Official bullion imports (including doré) fell 70% y/y to 64t in Q3, while net imports including unofficial flows were 114t, about 84% of India's 136t total supply.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Official import prints overstate the demand collapse; roughly 50t was off the books.

insights.claim: Domestic Indian gold traded at an average US$43/oz discount to import parity in Q3, the highest quarterly discount on record, attributed to unofficial inflows after the duty hike and to old-gold supply.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: A record discount is a market signal that the duty is being arbitraged, and it weakens the case for an official-channel import recovery.
insights.quote: The discount averaged US$43/oz in Q3, the highest quarterly level on record.

insights.claim: The WGC's econometric models find bar and coin demand is relatively more sensitive to duty changes and income than other segments, and the May duty hike likely contributed to the 40% y/y bar and coin drop.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Further duty changes would hit investment-grade bars and coins hardest; a duty cut would be a bullish catalyst for Indian investment demand.
insights.quote: bar and coin demand is relatively more sensitive to duty changes and income
insights.locator: Investment demand cools but stays resilient

insights.claim: Investment demand fell only 4% y/y in the first nine months of 2026 versus an 18% fall in jewellery, suggesting investment buying is less sensitive to high prices; investment was 42% of net demand in Q3, down from 69% in Q1 when it overtook jewellery.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Indian investors are structurally stickier gold buyers than jewellery consumers, but the Q1 investment-led peak was a momentum spike that has faded.
insights.locator: Investment demand cools but stays resilient

insights.claim: Indian gold ETF demand rose to 5.3t in Q3 from 3.6t in Q2, lifting holdings to about 124t, though still below the 17.6t of Q4'25 and 19.9t of Q1'26.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: ETF inflows continue on a lower slope, consistent with price momentum fading rather than a loss of interest.
insights.quote: point to sustained investor interest in gold

insights.claim: In mid-October mutual fund houses temporarily suspended fresh subscriptions to gold Fund of Funds, a segment whose AUM is about one-third of gold ETF AUM, although existing SIPs and direct ETF investment continue.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: FoF subscription curbs are a Q4 downside risk to Indian ETF flows, though the WGC expects the effect to be contained.
insights.quote: mutual fund houses temporarily suspended fresh subscriptions to gold Fund of Funds (FoFs)
insights.locator: Gold ETFs also continued to attract investment

insights.claim: Gross digital gold purchases in India reached about 4.9t in Q3 and 16.3t in nine months, up 76% from 9.2t, even as survey intent to buy digital gold fell from 38% to 34%.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Digital gold is a small but fast-growing channel; the dip in stated intent warns the growth may be slowing.
insights.locator: Investment is also broadening beyond traditional channels

insights.claim: The RBI bought just 0.3t of gold in the first nine months of 2026, versus 4t in the same period of 2025 and 50t in 9M'24, holding reserves roughly flat at about 880.5t; the RBI has moved from accumulation to maintenance.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: A major EM central bank buyer has stepped back at gold prices above US$4,000, removing one pillar of official-sector demand.
insights.quote: a shift from active reserve accumulation to maintenance of existing holdings

insights.claim: Gold's share of India's foreign reserves fell from 19% in January to 14.5% at end-Q3 despite near-flat tonnage, so the change reflects valuation and the broader reserve portfolio rather than selling.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: The reserve-share decline is mechanical, but a lower share can give the RBI room to resume buying if it wants a higher target.

insights.claim: In the WGC-Kantar survey, consumers expecting to increase jewellery purchases over three months rose from 20% to 29% and those expecting to reduce fell from 51% to 40%, while those expecting higher gold prices fell from 69% to 61%.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Intent improves as price-rise expectations soften, which suggests Indian buyers buy more when momentum cools.

insights.claim: Indian jewellery buyers are adapting to high prices: 77% say they would trade down on purity or carat (from 72%), 76% would exchange old jewellery to fund purchases (from 70%), and 39% will limit buying to festivals, auspicious periods or offers (from 33%).
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Lower-carat mix, old-gold exchange and occasion-driven buying are the price-adjustment mechanisms; expect weaker volume per rupee spent and more demand concentrated in the festive season.

insights.claim: Investment-led jewellery buying fell from 19% to 15% of survey respondents while wedding-driven intent rose from 22% to 25% and festival-driven from 16% to 21%, so jewellery demand is becoming more cultural and less speculative.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Jewellery demand is becoming less sensitive to gold price momentum and more tied to the wedding and festival calendar.

insights.claim: Recycled gold was only 19t (about 14% of supply) in Q3, down 12% y/y, despite domestic prices 45% higher; the WGC reads the muted recycling response as holders refusing to sell and possibly expecting further price upside.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Low scrap supply at record prices signals strong holder conviction and limits a supply response that would cap prices.
insights.quote: This behaviour could indicate expectations of further price upside.

insights.claim: The Q3 y/y decline is exaggerated by a festive calendar shift: festivals that supported Q3 2025 demand fall in October-December this year, so some demand and deferred imports move into Q4.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Expect Q4 y/y comparisons and official imports to improve mechanically as the festive and wedding season lands.
insights.quote: festivals that supported demand in Q3 last year occurring in the October–December quarter this year

insights.claim: The WGC expects seasonal festive and wedding buying to support Q4, but elevated prices and a weak rural economy after a poor monsoon should temper demand, with investment demand positive yet sensitive to price momentum.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: Q4 should be a sequential recovery in volumes but not a return to 2025 levels.
insights.quote: weakness in the rural economy following a poor monsoon are likely to temper demand

insights.claim: India accounted for 32% of global jewellery consumption in Q3 and 27% over nine months, and about 21% of global Q3 bar and coin demand, second only to China in bars and coins.
insights.speaker: Kavita Chacko
insights.so_what: India's swings are a first-order driver of global physical gold demand.
insights.locator: India remained the world's largest jewellery market
